title: Hangul Basics: Syllable Blocks
description: Learn how Korean syllables are organized into blocks
explanation:
# How Hangul Works

Unlike English (which reads left to right) or Arabic (which reads right to left), Korean syllables are organized into **square blocks**.

## Syllable Structure

Each block contains:
- **Initial consonant** (자음) — top left or left
- **Vowel** (모음) — top right or right
- **Final consonant** (종성) — bottom (optional)

### Examples:

| Character | Components | Meaning |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| **가** | ㄱ + ㅏ | go |
| **나** | ㄴ + ㅏ | I, me |
| **닭** | ㄷ + ㅏ + ㄹ | chicken |

## Why Blocks?

Hangul's **square design** is genius because:
1. **Easy to read** — all syllables are the same size
2. **Easy to type** — syllables fit naturally on keyboards
3. **Makes sense** — the shapes relate to mouth positions!

## Reading Order

Read each block like this:
1. Top-to-bottom
2. Left-to-right (within the block)

So **가** reads: top-left (ㄱ) → right (ㅏ) = "ga"

---

💡 **Pro tip:** Every Korean syllable you'll ever see fits into this block pattern. Master this, and you're ready to learn!

exercises.prompt: Which part of 나 is the vowel?
exercises.explanationIfWrong: The vowel ㅏ is on the right side of the block.
